column1: # The Dynamo parity exclusions (E11-T23 step B, DYNAMO-COVERAGE §7).
# The reverse direction of the parity manifest: of every public member of Spark.Geometry, either a
# row of dynamo-parity.tsv names it, or this file says why no row needs to. A member that is neither
# is counted against the residue budget at the foot of this file.
# IT EXCUSES BY RULE AND NEVER MEMBER BY MEMBER. Spark.Geometry declares 877 public members by the
# manifest's own counting rule - methods, properties, enum values and operators, and not constructors
# or property accessors - and 778 of them are named by no row today. A file holding 778 hand-written
# excuses would be the drifting artefact §7 exists to prevent. Two scopes do the work - a member-name
# rule that applies on any type, and a whole type Dynamo has no counterpart for - and what neither
# reaches is counted rather than waved through. 44 rules today: 5 member names and 39 types.
#   MemberName  Name is a member name, or op_* for the operators. Excused wherever it appears.
#   Type        Name is a full type name. Refused if any parity row names one of its members.
#   Budget      Name is "residue"; Reason begins with the count. The check requires an EXACT match,
#               so the number falls as rows are assessed and cannot quietly climb back.

An explicit tolerance value, passed to every operation that needs one (ADR-0010). Dynamo uses ambient tolerances, which is what this type exists not to do.
An analytic torus. As PlaneSurface.
Spark's 4x4 matrix. Dynamo has no such type - it puts the whole transformation algebra on CoordinateSystem, which §3.1 records as the largest deliberate shape difference in the value layer.
A 2D vector. Dynamo has no 2D vector type; UV is its nearest and is a parameter pair, not a direction.

287 members are named by no row and excused by no rule. They are not excusable: they sit on types that DO map to a Dynamo type, so each one is either a member some Unassessed row will name once it is assessed, or a genuine gap. The check requires an EXACT match, so the number falls as rows are assessed and cannot quietly climb back. IT ROSE ONCE, FROM 278 TO 287 ON 2026-09-12, AND THE REASON IS RECORDED RATHER THAN ABSORBED: E2-T44 assessed §3.5 and 13 Spark members became named by a row - which took three whole types, BrepFaceView, BrepLoopView and BrepEdgeView, out of the excused list, because a type a row names cannot be excused wholesale. Their remaining members joined the residue. A rise with no such entry beside it means a member was added to a mapped type with no thought for the register.
